body: ASG ran the Book Exchanger for a third semester, a free listing publication in which students advertised used textbooks to each other as an alternative to selling back to the bookstore. Cards went into student mailboxes on 11 November with a 20 November deadline, and about 60 students listed books each semester. Student Affairs chairman Victor Click said the project raised about $60 the previous fall and nothing in the spring against printing costs of about $653, that the year's budget allotted $750 to it, and that he would recommend dropping it if this run failed.
money: $750 budgeted; about $653 spent on printing the previous year; about $60 raised

title: The Angie Norcia Award is created for the yearly banquet
body: At the 9 February meeting student government created an award to present at its yearly banquet in May, named for Angie Norcia, an Owensboro senior who had died the previous summer of adult respiratory distress syndrome and Guillain-Barre syndrome and who had been active in student government for more than two years. President Tim Todd said it would be one of the highest honours given to a congress member, with recipients nominated and interviewed by a committee of members. It survived as the Mary Angela Norcia Memorial Award, still on the banquet nomination list in 1994.

title: ASG backs the Frankfort rally for higher education
body: ASG suspended its rules on 9 February to adopt the standard resolution urging Governor Wallace Wilkinson and the legislature to fund higher education, and presented it at the Frankfort rally on 16 February; Western's was the last of the eight state student governments to pass it. About 3,000 students, faculty and alumni marched up Capitol Avenue in what the Kentucky Advocates for Higher Education called the largest Frankfort demonstration since 1964. Western sent four free buses and 130 of the 161 people who signed up made the trip, joining a Western contingent of about 250, with cheerleaders handing out 250 red towels. A Herald editorial the same week said ASG had choked by passing only a form resolution while Murray State's government ran a write-a-thon that got more than 500 students to write the governor.

title: International Day, co-sponsored with the University Center Board
body: More than 800 high school students from around the state came to Western on Friday 25 October for the annual International Day, sponsored by the University Center Board, Associated Student Government, International Programs and Student Affairs. A bazaar on the third floor of Downing University Center sold handmade goods from other countries, including bracelets, ornaments, scarves and belts made by Indian tribes in Ecuador and African woodwork and silver and copper jewellery. Profits from the crafts went to Escuela Para Padres, a joint fundraising organisation working to prevent abuse of women and children; project coordinator Joan Martin said jewellery was the best seller.

title: Voter registration drive signs up nearly 1,000 students
body: ASG ran a voter registration drive for the 5 November 1991 election, led by vice president John Seiber, who with other congress members registered nearly 1,000 Western students. A full-page ASG advertisement in the Herald the following February listed the drive alongside fall break, campus recycling, organizational aid, new picnic tables, a new copier for the science library and the radio show as the year's work, with forums on the election, student concerns, the class presidents and a question and answer session with the regents.

title: A permanent voter registration booth at class registration
body: Bill 92-06-S, introduced on 24 March 1992 by Trent Lyda for the Legislative Research Committee, committed ASG to keeping a voter registration booth wherever class registration took place each fall and spring, to capitalise on the influx of unregistered eligible student voters. The committee was to coordinate the scheduling of students and organisations willing to staff it, and every ASG member was asked to work the booth for at least an hour during the registration period.

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 92-06-S, Establishment of Permanent Voter Registration Program

title: Sixteen thousand savings cards and a Vote About It drive
body: At the first meeting of the year President Joe Rains reported that sixteen thousand student savings cards were ready for distribution, and public relations vice president Patrick Monahan told members they could begin handing them out. Administrative vice president Susan Mitchell, chairing the Vote America committee, announced a voter registration drive for mid-September and a later drive on absentee voting under the theme VOTE ABOUT IT. The same meeting recorded the summer's new SGA logo, new furniture and a computer, and the loss of the agency account that had let the organisation buy things as it needed them.

title: Forums between congress members and hall governments
body: Bill 92-05-F, introduced 6 October 1992 and passed unanimously on 13 October, set up forums between on-campus residents and SGA in conjunction with the hall governments. The reasoning was that congress members attending hall government meetings could answer questions hall officers could not, and that the on-campus population made up a significant part of the student body.

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 92-05-F, Establishing Forums Between Campus Residents and SGA

title: Adopt-A-Spot put on a contract footing
body: Bill 92-09-F, introduced by Eric McWilliams and Kevin Moore on 20 October 1992 and passed unanimously, had SGA finance and run an Adopt-A-Spot programme in which student organisations took contractual responsibility for keeping a designated patch of campus clean. The Campus Improvements Committee oversaw the scheme and divided the university into geographical areas, and of the more than 120 student organisations on campus many were judged to have the numbers to look after a spot. Groups that failed to do what they had agreed were required to make complete restitution to SGA.

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 92-09-F, Contractual Agreement for Adopt-a-Spot Program

title: SGA puts $100 behind the Topperettes' trip to Dallas
body: Bill 92-14-F, introduced 1 December 1992, joined SGA with other university departments in contributing one hundred dollars towards sending the WKU Topperettes to the national competition in Dallas in early January. The bill said the squad enhanced student life at Western with their skills and had worked hard to qualify. The team finished ninth in the nation, and the SGA secretary reported in January that a letter of congratulation had been sent.

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 92-14-F, Funding for Topperettes

title: President for a Day raffle tickets go on sale
body: At the 19 January 1993 meeting the administrative vice president's office reported that raffle tickets for President for a Day were going on sale that week, and tickets were handed out to congress members to sell. Public relations vice president Patrick Monahan pressed members to sell a lot of them. The same report noted that the radio show with President Joe Rains would now go out live rather than taped.

title: Head Start at congress, and members sent out to volunteer
body: Dr Jerry Wilder and Mike Gramling, director of the Head Start programme, were the guest speakers at the 12 October 1993 congress meeting. Public relations chairwoman Emily Brown then encouraged members to volunteer for Head Start. The treasurer reported the account balance that night at $38,977.50 with no expenditures since the previous meeting, and organizational aid interviews were being held on 12 and 13 October.

title: Word on Western named as the SGA radio show
body: Public relations chairwoman Emily Brown told congress on 12 October 1993 that Word on Western would be the name of the SGA radio show, to be heard on 91.7 FM at 2 p.m. on Wednesdays. It followed the taped and then live show the previous administration had run under Joe Rains. The same meeting heard that Adopt-A-Spot places were still open and that articles for the SGA newsletter, The Gavel, were due by 25 October.

title: $150 for a Book Exchanger board in Downing University Center
body: Bill 93-5-F, by Jill Reading and Eddie Myers for the Student Affairs Committee, allocated $150 to buy a large bulletin board and sign where students could list by category the books they wanted to sell. The board was to go on the first floor of Downing University Center across from the Marriott office. The bill argued that inflated book prices and minimal buy-back prices left students needing a place to sell to each other.

title: Angelo Rodriguez serves as President for a Day
body: President Donald Smith congratulated Angelo Rodriguez at the 22 February 1994 meeting for serving as President for a Day. Smith also reported that the Frankfort reception had gone well with seventy legislators attending and fifteen Western students present. The treasurer put expenditures since the last meeting at $320.62, leaving a balance of $21,139.97.

title: Cultural Diversity Week and Spirit Week in preparation
body: Administrative vice president Scott Sivley reported on 22 February 1994 that Cultural Diversity Week was almost set and that the Adopt-A-Spot committee would meet on 24 February. Public relations vice president Bert Blevins reported that letters were going out to all organisations about Spirit Week. Both weeks were SGA-run additions to the spring calendar alongside the campus clean-up and President for a Day.

title: The Points of Light programme and The Polaris
body: Bill 94-4-S, by Donald Smith and Scott Sivley, created the Points of Light programme to honour students who gave their time to help society, open to nomination by any campus organisation or individual and awarded by the executive officers at intervals through the year. Recipients were named in the Herald, given a certificate and honoured at SGA's annual banquet. The most outstanding recipient received an annual award called The Polaris, a commemorative plaque and a $100 SGA donation to the charity of their choice.
money: $100 donated to the Polaris winner's chosen charity

src.label: SGA Records, Bill 94-4-S, Points of Light Program

title: Nominations open for the year-end SGA awards
body: At the 29 March 1994 meeting the secretary took nominations for the year's awards: the Citizen's Award, Outstanding Congress Member, Outstanding Committee Member, the Dero Downing Award, the Kerrie Faye Stewart Memorial Award, the Mary Angela Norcia Memorial Award and the Dean Charles A. Keown Award. She also handed out certificates to past Committee and Congress Members of the Month. The banquet was set for 26 April at 6 p.m. in the Kentucky Museum.

title: Memorial trees, recycling bins and the book exchange board in hand
body: The 29 March 1994 meeting recorded Bowling Green Operation Pride agreeing to help find donated trees for the SGA memorial tree programme for students who died while enrolled. Campus Improvements reported that Coca-Cola was donating ten bins for aluminium can recycling, that Adopt-A-Spot winners would be announced that week, and that the grievance boards had been dropped. Student Affairs reported it was working on the Book Exchanger board.
money: ten aluminium recycling bins donated by Coca-Cola

title: The executive officers veto the homecoming queen idea
body: A week after Congress voted to enter a homecoming queen candidate, SGA's executive officers vetoed the plan. The candidacy never happened.

src.label: Herald 70:12, 29 Sep 1994 - Quarles, "Student Government Association Officers Veto Homecoming Queen Idea"

title: The book exchange takes on the bookstore
body: SGA ran a book exchange to let students buy and sell textbooks among themselves rather than through the College Heights Bookstore. The Herald headlined it as SGA helping students avoid the bookstore blues.

src.label: Herald 70:13, 4 Oct 1994 - Hutchins, "Student Government Association Helps Students Avoid Bookstore Blues - Book Exchange"

title: Child-care grants awarded to student parents
body: SGA awarded child-care grants to students enrolled in the WKU child care program, a standing service the organisation funded out of its own budget and disbursed by committee each year. The same issue reported a public relations bill that failed.

title: A new SGA award honours Sam Sharbutt
body: SGA created an award named for Sam Sharbutt in the autumn of 1994. It joined the set of recognitions the organisation handed out at its year-end banquet.

src.label: Herald 70:14, 13 Oct 1994 - "New Student Government Association Award Honors Sam Sharbutt"

title: Bill 94-9-F establishes a series of public forums
body: Lena Sweeten's bill committed SGA to hold public forums at least three times a semester so students could raise concerns directly. It passed on second reading on 22 November 1994 and set the pattern for the forum programme SGA ran for the next decade.

title: Big Red Days and 500 red towels
body: Jason Young's Bill 94-10-F created Big Red Days, asking the whole student body to wear red on days Western played a men's or women's home basketball game. It directed SGA members to hand out 500 red towels costing $1.00 each at the games, and was written to revive the spirit of the E. A. Diddle era.

title: Two people show up for the campus clean-up
body: SGA's December 1994 campus clean-up drew two volunteers. The Herald reported the turnout the following day under the headline "Only Two Show for Yesterday's Clean-Up."

title: WKU: Helping Us Help You links students to local employers
body: Bill 95-1-S created a partnership between SGA and Bowling Green businesses to increase part-time employment for WKU students. Businesses with 15 or more employees were measured twice a year on the share of WKU students they hired, and the winner was thanked with a half-page Herald advertisement and a sign in Downing University Center.

body: SGA's campus clean-up opened on 23 February 1995. The Herald ran a notice the morning it started.

title: Nearly 150 workers turn out for the clean-up
body: The February 1995 clean-up drew close to 150 volunteers, a reversal of the two-person turnout of the previous December. The Herald reported the count five days after the event began.

title: Organizational Aid pays out $2,500 to thirteen groups
body: Bill 95-2-S disbursed the $2,500 budgeted for Organizational Aid after the committee spent more than eight hours across four meetings. Recipients included Kappa Alpha Psi and Delta Sigma Theta at $250 each, Habitat for Humanity at $225, and the Topperettes at $175.

title: Faculty or Staff Member of the Month and Year awards created

title: Resolution 95-6-S asks for an annual Sibling's Day
body: Carlene and Darlene Lodmell's resolution requested a Sibling's Day each spring, arguing that siblings under 18 had no way to visit campus without a parent while Parents' Day covered the autumn. The resolution asked that it be timed to coincide with Coming Home activities.

title: The last clean-up of the year

title: Faculty Appreciation Day set for 23 April 1998

title: The first Meet Your Dean Reception, 7 April 1998

title: $300 to the second Women of Western Conference
body: Bill 98-4-F contributed $300 to the second annual Women of Western (W.O.W.) Conference. The conference paired a keynote address with workshops on women's issues, leadership and communication, presented in part by WKU faculty and staff.

title: Pride Week coffee house in Niteclass
body: SGA co-sponsored a coffee house with the African-American Players on Thursday 5 November 1998 at 9.30 p.m. in Niteclass, to mark Pride Week. Bill 98-5-F described it as a place for students to share their creative talents and as the academic component of the week.

title: SGA co-sponsors the 1999 Camp Fair
body: Bill 98-13-F committed SGA to co-sponsor the 1999 Camp Fair with the Career Services Center on 4 February 1999 in Downing University Center. Over 100 companies were to be invited, and the bill noted that the previous year's fair had drawn positive comment from employers and students.

title: Faculty Appreciation Day and the Excellence in Teaching Award
body: Bill 99-1-S set 11 March 1999 as Faculty Appreciation Day with a catered reception at the Faculty House at 4 p.m. The reception was chosen as the occasion to present the Teacher Excellence Award to the outstanding faculty member of the year.

title: Excellence in Teaching Award opened to all six colleges

title: $300 toward the KASWE conference on campus
body: Bill 99-12-S contributed $300 to the WKU Student Social Workers Organization to help host the Kentucky Association of Social Work Educators conference on 8 and 9 April 1999. title: A co-ed volleyball tournament before finals
body: Bill 99-19-S allocated up to $350 for a co-ed volleyball tournament on 22 and 23 April 1999. The authors wanted a recreational event to bring students together in the run-up to finals.

title: The electronic sign money is turned into a stage

title: A coffee house in Helm Library for finals week

title: Library hours pushed to 2 a.m. for finals

title: An autumn campus clean-up on 18 October 1999

title: Earth Day week clean-up, 20 April 2000

title: A month of free USA Today in the residence halls

title: Post-homecoming clean-up, 17 October 2000

title: The First Union Campus Spirit Award, a $16,500 prize package

title: Campus clean-up on 23 April 2001
body: Bill 01-4-S set a campus-wide clean-up for 3.30 p.m. on Monday 23 April 2001, marking Earth Day. Attending organisations earned community service hours and points toward the First Union Hilltopper Athletic Foundation Spirit Award.

title: Go With the Flow extended and umbrellas added to the lending shelf
body: On 11 November 2025 SGA announced a bill extending Go With the Flow, the programme it created to put free menstrual products in campus bathrooms, by supplying a full box expected to last the rest of the semester and adding a donation box for toothbrushes, toothpaste and soap. Senator Caroline Yates, who wrote it, called menstrual products a basic need. A second bill that passed the same night funded borrowable umbrellas from the SGA office, lent like the calculators.
